body.x: GEVR Co., Ltd. (CEO Do JungGug) announced its participation in CES 2025 from January 7 to 10 in Las Vegas through the K-Startup Pavilion.

The company specializes in evaluating, managing, and servicing batteries used in devices such as drones, electric vehicles, e-scooters, e-bikes, power tools, and wireless appliances. It also develops and markets fire suppression devices for battery-related fires.

GEVR’s offerings include the GV-Series, EV-Guard L/U (fire suppression devices for lithium battery fires for lower and upper areas), and certification training for battery-related skills. The company holds one trademark, two registered patents, and two pending patents. In 2024, GEVR registered its factory, established the “Battery Fire Safety Research Institute” to develop applicable suppression liquids, and received certification for its fire suppression agents. The company was recognized with the Technical Innovation Award at K-Battery Show 2024.
Since 2020, GEVR has partnered with the Korea EV Technology Association to provide monthly certification training for battery performance evaluators, resulting in over 1,100 certified professionals.

At CES 2025, GEVR will unveil EV-Guard, which consists of a piercing device, controller, and fire suppression system. The piercing device is equipped with motors that allow it to move remotely over 10 meters using a mobile application. It autonomously navigates under vehicles to perform precise piercing. The drill utilizes a proprietary dual-blade design with adjustable angles, powered by four 500W motors. These motors are supported by a reliable automotive-grade secondary battery (100Ah), which undergoes regular performance checks to ensure safety and reliability.

The controller powers the motors and offers additional backup options with AC220V or AC110V for emergencies. It integrates an in-house algorithm that adjusts the drilling motor's operations based on load conditions. The entire operation, from deployment to piercing, takes approximately five minutes, followed by fire suppression, which takes about 15 minutes. The included suppression liquid, supplied in 25L quantities, takes three minutes to discharge completely.

body.x: GEVR explained that the batteries used in their fire suppression tests were 4.1V pouch-type SK and LG batteries tested in cell or module configurations. The average fire suppression time was around 10 minutes, and the success rate was 80% under varying conditions such as battery charge levels, battery quantity, and suppression liquid specifications.

The company expressed its ambition to expand into international markets, including the United States and China. “Through exports, we aim to widely promote the agents and products we’ve developed, contributing to a culture of safe battery usage worldwide,” stated CEO Do JungGug.

AVING News, covering CES for 19 consecutive years, continues to bridge the gap for Korean SMEs and startups looking to expand globally. AVING's international media partners will cover these programs.
